title: DRAFT: Reading a dose-volume histogram (OpenKBP personal use, unpublishable)
review_status: DRAFT pending review by a domain expert. OpenKBP data is for personal hackathon use only and this lesson cannot be published.
learning_objectives: Read a cumulative DVH: the fraction of a structure receiving at least a given dose.
Compare target and organ-at-risk curves on the same plot.
Explain why a benchmark reference dose is not a delivered treatment plan.
rubric: DRAFT rubric pending review by a domain expert. Reward accurate reading of the curve, not treatment judgements.

rubric_criteria.title: Reading the DVH
rubric_criteria.description: Correctly reads volume fractions at chosen doses.

rubric_criteria.title: Target versus organ at risk
rubric_criteria.description: Describes how target and organ-at-risk curves differ.

rubric_criteria.title: Limits
rubric_criteria.description: States that this is benchmark data and not a treatment plan.

blocks.title: Learning objectives
blocks.content: Read a cumulative DVH, compare target and organ-at-risk curves, and explain why a benchmark reference dose is not a delivered plan.

blocks.title: What you are looking at
blocks.content: This is an OpenKBP benchmark case on a processed voxel grid. The dose is a reference used for research benchmarking, not a delivered treatment plan, and no patient orientation is implied.

blocks.title: Open the DVH
blocks.content: Select a target (for example PTV70) and an organ at risk (for example the spinal cord) and read their DVH curves.

blocks.title: Read the curve
blocks.content: What percentage of the chosen target receives at least 95% of its prescription dose, according to the curve?

blocks.title: Compare two structures
blocks.content: How does the organ-at-risk curve differ in shape from the target curve, and why would a planner want that?

blocks.title: State a limit
blocks.content: Name one reason this benchmark dose cannot be read as a real patient's treatment.
